title: Exploring the Investigative World of Science

topics.title: From wonder to investigation: the root and the kite

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that Grade 8 science aims at learning how to find new facts through focused questions, simple experiments and observation.
Interpret the root and kite symbols as the balance between careful observation and creative thinking.

topics.title: The journey ahead: microbes, health, electricity, force and pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that microorganisms can be helpful or harmful and that food, exercise, medicines and vaccines keep us healthy.
Identify the heating and magnetic effects of electric current and their everyday uses.
Relate force and pressure to how air moves, from gentle breezes to cyclones.
Describe how particles move in solids and gases and classify materials as elements, compounds and mixtures.
Recognise that light reflects from mirrors and rough surfaces and bends when it passes through lenses.

topics.title: Moon, calendars, ecosystems and a planet just right for life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the Moon's phases depend on the positions of the Earth, Moon and Sun and helped humans make calendars.
Describe how living beings depend on their surroundings and why Earth is suited to life.
Evaluate the role of human activities and science in changing and protecting Earth's climate.

topics.title: Investigating like a scientist: why does a puri puff up?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors that can be changed or controlled in a simple kitchen experiment.
Distinguish yes/no observations from measured quantities and value careful record-keeping.
Apply the rule of changing only one factor at a time while keeping other conditions the same.
